paper.title: Adapt as You Say: Online Interactive Bimanual Skill Adaptation via Human Language Feedback
paper.source_version: arXiv v1, submitted 2026-03-27; only public arXiv version verified 2026-08-30. PDF SHA-256 09a1f67c76a2b9ffce0999677a83d6ad36a49c3c30c3bddecfb4fada29687b7a; source-archive SHA-256 e23fe4268917f2012ca69f6100ec9886fa4b507c76c490924b9fa8654fac62f2. Official project repository pinned at commit fde0c830ce32cba3905da889189aff3cc573c658 (2026-03-13); it contains project-page/media assets and a placeholder code link, not the BiSAIL method implementation.

decision_relevance.why_admitted: BiSAIL source-locates a decoupled interface that turns language plus visual/embodiment context into a trajectory-scoring objective and a closed coordination label, then uses post-execution feedback to revise both. This informs Sam's steering schema and validation protocol while sharply bounding what cannot count as a reference-oracle or executable-task-reward intervention under the fixed trainer.
not_evidence_for: selection, cropping, ordering, splicing, transition logic, or certification of immutable reference clips
a bounded per-step executable task reward consumed by an unchanged RL trainer
an oracle-only or task-reward-only intervention under a fixed controller, observation, action, dynamics, and budget contract
zero-update cross-embodiment portability, because the Franka BMP is retrained
dynamic adaptation of speed, acceleration, or interaction forces
an independent objective-reward validator, calibrated success gate, or safe generated-code execution boundary
availability of a reproducible BiSAIL method implementation, checkpoints, training data, or evaluation code

mechanisms.name: Embodied language-to-objective compiler
mechanisms.description: A four-step MLLM reasoning chain combines language feedback, visual task context, end-effector/object keypoints, and bimanual taxonomy knowledge to emit a non-differentiable trajectory reward R(tau;l,o) plus one of six coordination categories.

mechanisms.name: Task-agnostic bimanual diffusion prior
mechanisms.description: An unconditional encoder-only Transformer diffusion model is trained with diffusion, pairwise-diversity, and second-order smoothness losses on one million URDF-generated, reachability-checked, collision-filtered bimanual motions to supply online proposals beyond one task's demonstrations.

mechanisms.name: Black-box reward-guided diffusion search
mechanisms.description: Thirty-two BMP proposals are scored by the generated black-box objective, resampled through a temperature-weighted distribution, mutated by truncated forward diffusion, and denoised for four search iterations before the best-scoring trajectory is selected.

mechanisms.name: Product-of-experts bimanual motion modulation
mechanisms.description: Within truncated denoising, annealed MCMC combines the pretrained BMP score, an offline task-specific diffusion-policy score, and a coordination-energy gradient so the adapted trajectory remains near the task distribution while satisfying the inferred interaction pattern.

mechanisms.name: Post-execution objective reflection loop
mechanisms.description: The same ESA-CoT/MLLM consumes the original and adapted motions, post-execution language/visual context, and prior reasoning history to revise the trajectory reward and emit a binary success indicator; execution and reflection repeat until success or an unspecified retry cap.

failure_modes.name: Kinematic-only adaptation boundary
failure_modes.description: The reported method changes spatial motions only; it cannot adapt execution speed, acceleration, or interaction force.

failure_modes.name: Generated objectives do not fail closed
failure_modes.description: Full ESA-CoT reports 89.8% executability, leaving roughly one in ten benchmark rewards non-executable; the differentiable-reward variant reports 42.9%. The paper does not define a typed reward language, static checks, sandbox, or promotion gate.

failure_modes.name: Generator and stop judge share one MLLM
failure_modes.description: The same ESA-CoT/MLLM revises the objective reward and emits the binary success indicator used to stop retries, so promotion is not grounded in an independent evaluator.

failure_modes.name: Task-policy proposals trade diversity for feasibility
failure_modes.description: Initial proposals sampled from the plate-wiping task policy remain close to the demonstrations; increasing noise or reducing observation conditioning adds diversity but produces jerky or physically implausible motions.

failure_modes.name: Alternative composition samplers leave the joint distribution
failure_modes.description: Removing MCMC lowers task and coordination scores, classifier guidance degrades when g rises from 300 to 500, and removing BMP noise collapses intent alignment to 32.3%, exposing sensitivity to the sampling mechanism.

failure_modes.name: Core runtime and reward contracts are underspecified
failure_modes.description: v1 gives no values for BMP loss weights, selection temperature, mutation depth, MCMC guide ratio or schedules, retry cap, task-policy training details, generated-reward schema, exact prompt/model snapshot, or end-to-end adaptation latency.

failure_modes.name: Human and uncertainty protocols are incomplete
failure_modes.description: The reasoning set is expert annotated and tables report plus/minus values, but v1 does not report expert count or agreement, metric raters, repeated model-call seeds, the meaning of plus/minus, or end-to-end retry/latency statistics.

failure_modes.name: Inference-time motion synthesis exceeds the two-knob boundary
failure_modes.description: BiSAIL requires a newly trained task-agnostic diffusion prior, score access to an offline task-specific diffusion policy, and a new trajectory-generation/sampling path; its Franka study retrains BMP. These are not a reference-oracle or executable-training-reward substitution under Sam's fixed trainer.

failure_modes.name: Claimed code is not publicly released
failure_modes.description: Although arXiv v1 says code is available, the latest pinned official repository contains project-page and media assets only; its code button is marked coming soon and targets a placeholder URL.

evaluation.name: Held-out multimodal objective-reasoning evaluation
evaluation.description: On 100 held-out language-plus-image task variations after 20 prompt demonstrations, full ESA-CoT reports 93.7% reasoning accuracy, 89.8% reward executability, and 0.94 ROUGE-L, outperforming prompting baselines and six reported variants.

evaluation.name: Bimanual motion-prior architecture evaluation
evaluation.description: BMP is compared with U-Net, decoder-only, encoder-decoder, and no-auxiliary variants using FID, diversity, smoothness, and sampling time; the reported full BMP result is 2.48 FID, 0.93 diversity, 0.02 smoothness, and 0.16 seconds.

evaluation.name: Online motion-modulation ablation
evaluation.description: On bowl shelving with ten ESA-CoT objectives and twenty trials per method, full BMM reports 86.8% intent alignment, 82.5% task alignment, and 83.9% constraint satisfaction against ranking, CEM, MPPI, no-MCMC, classifier-guided, and no-BMP-noise variants.

evaluation.name: Six-task language-guided real-robot comparison
evaluation.description: Across six DOBOT tasks and object, environmental, and human-preference variations, BiSAIL reports mean TSR 0.77, 0.77, and 0.76 against DP, ACT, IDMP, DSRL, YAY, and LATTE full-pipeline baselines.

evaluation.name: Franka embodiment adaptation evaluation
evaluation.description: After retraining BMP for a dual-arm Franka platform, the paper reports four-task intent alignment of 71.5–82.7%, task alignment of 73.3–84.2%, and constraint satisfaction of 67.8–83.6%.

evidence.locator: Title block, abstract, comments, and submission history
evidence.claim: The record identifies eight authors, a 27 March 2026 v1 submission, eleven pages, and links the official project page; v1 is the only public arXiv version verified on 30 August 2026.

BiSAIL optimizes an N-by-D sequence of dual-arm pose/gripper actions under a product of task-agnostic motion prior, offline task-specific diffusion policy, language-conditioned trajectory reward, and coordination energy.

ESA-CoT combines user-intent grounding, visual task-context analysis, embodied keypoints, objective reasoning, and a six-category bimanual taxonomy to emit a non-differentiable black-box reward plus coordination class.

evidence.locator: Section IV-B, Equations 12-15, Figures 5-6, and Data Generation paragraph
evidence.claim: BMP is an encoder-only unconditional diffusion model with diversity and smoothness losses, trained on one million URDF-driven, reachability-checked, collision-filtered bimanual motions.

evidence.locator: Section IV-C, Equations 16-26, Algorithm 1, and Figure 7
evidence.claim: Online modulation reward-scores, resamples, diffuses, and denoises BMP proposals, then uses annealed MCMC to combine BMP and task-policy scores with coordination-energy gradients before selecting the best trajectory.

The same ESA-CoT/MLLM receives original/adapted motions, post-execution language/vision context, and reasoning history, then returns a revised reward and binary success bit; retries stop at success or an unspecified maximum.

evidence.locator: Section V-A, Implementation Details and Task Settings
evidence.claim: The experiments use GPT-4o at temperature 0.2; AdamW at learning rate 1e-4 and batch 256; 32 proposals; four search and four MCMC steps; ten denoising steps; one RTX 4090 workstation; and a dual-Nova2 DOBOT platform for six tasks.

The 120-case expert-annotated reasoning set uses 20 prompt demonstrations and 100 evaluation cases; full ESA-CoT reports 93.7% RA, 89.8% ER, and 0.94 ROUGE-L, while the differentiable-reward variant reports 66.5%, 42.9%, and 0.91.

evidence.locator: Section V-C, Table II, and Figures 11-12
evidence.claim: Task-policy proposals overfit demonstrations and become jerky or implausible when diversity is forced; full BMP reports 2.48 FID, 0.93 diversity, 0.02 smoothness, and 0.16-second sampling time.

evidence.locator: Section V-D, Table III, and Figure 10
evidence.claim: On bowl shelving with ten objectives and twenty trials per method, full BMM reports 86.8/82.5/83.9% IA/TA/CS; no-MCMC, classifier-guided, and no-BMP-noise variants expose task, coordination, distribution-shift, and diversity failures.

evidence.locator: Section V-E, Table IV, and Figures 13-14
evidence.claim: Six-task DOBOT experiments compare six baselines under object, environmental, and preference variations using fifteen random language feedback per variation type; BiSAIL reports mean TSR 0.77, 0.77, and 0.76.

evidence.locator: Section V-F, Table V, and Figure 15
evidence.claim: For four dual-arm Franka tasks, BMP is retrained for the embodiment and the reported IA/TA/CS ranges are 71.5-82.7%, 73.3-84.2%, and 67.8-83.6%.
The authors identify kinematic-only adaptation as a limitation and name speed, acceleration, and interaction-force modulation as future work.

evidence.locator: Sections IV-B-IV-D, Equations 15-27, Algorithm 1, and Section V-A
evidence.claim: v1 leaves BMP loss weights, proposal temperature, mutation depth, MCMC guide ratio and schedules, maximum retries, task-policy training details, generated-reward schema and validation, exact GPT-4o snapshot/prompt, and end-to-end latency unspecified.
